headings.title: SMTO-CFG-0013 — SMTO can't save a name with hidden characters or a web address

html:
SMTO-CFG-0013 — SMTO can't save a name with hidden characters or a web address

GUID: 16072fad-4558-4bf0-a801-39d67d53561f
Slug: composer-name-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The name includes something that isn't plain text, such as a tab, a line break or an invisible character copied from elsewhere, or it looks like a web address. SMTO didn't save it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were changing Agent name in Settings › General › UI Preferences, delete the name and type it again by hand instead of pasting it. Pasted text often carries tabs or invisible characters, and SMTO won't show those in a name used on every screen.
  2. If you don't need a custom name, leave Agent name empty. An empty Agent name is always accepted and shows the product name instead.
  3. If a tool or script sent this message, ask its owner to remove line breaks, hidden characters and web addresses (anything with ://) from the Gateway name it sends. That Gateway name travels with the message, and SMTO refuses it before starting any work.

What success looks like

  • The new Agent name stays after you leave Settings and appears across SMTO, or your message is sent without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep saving the same pasted text; it will be refused each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A name field failed validation: the Agent name preference (agent_name) contains control characters (code points below 32 or 127–159) or U+2028/U+2029, or the composer's gateway_label_hint contains control characters or a '://' URL marker.

What this means

  • Composer text contains rejected control characters or a connection-URL marker; agent-name normalization also rejects Unicode line separators/control ranges. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Composer text contains rejected control characters or a connection-URL marker; agent-name normalization also rejects Unicode line separators/control ranges.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact field's single-line display-name rules without moving connection details into the name.

How to fix it

  • For agent_name (Settings › General › UI Preferences), strip characters below code point 32, 127–159 and U+2028/U+2029 before saving. For composer submissions, send a single-line gateway_label_hint (up to 240 characters) with no control characters or '://'.
  • Use a single-line display name without connection URLs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended plain display name passes its field validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
